svg.aria-label: A flow chart for making a game design document: narrow the question, answer five questions on paper, check whether a sentence would do, pick an archetype, sketch, draw, mark every part, check it reads standing up, then date it and pin it up.
svg.title: How to make a game design document
svg.desc: A decision flow with two exits, a branch into six page archetypes, and a loop back, so the process is drawn rather than listed.

g.inkscape:label: 10 Title
g.text: HOW TO MAKE A DESIGN DOCUMENT
The goal is to communicate an idea. It is not to produce documentation. Everything below follows from that.

g.inkscape:label: 20 Flow
g.text: You have one thing to communicate
On paper. With a pen. Before drawing anything.
Question five is the one everybody skips
and stop. That was the document.
defends a sketch, so it gets corrected.
One dominant illustration. Callouts on leaders,
in place. A sidebar. A description. Whitespace.
On the wall, beside the work

g.inkscape:label: 30 Archetypes
a sequence
g.text: Storyboard grid. The same frame repeated, banded by phase.

g.inkscape:label: a space
g.text: Annotated map, or a level sheet. Add a time ruler for pacing.

g.inkscape:label: a vocabulary
g.text: Taxonomy sheet. Strip the actors to tokens or the example

g.inkscape:label: a tradeoff
g.text: Constraint triangle. Put the governing rules in the empty centre.

g.inkscape:label: a relationship
g.text: Module map, screen flow, or state machine. Label every arrow.

g.inkscape:label: a comparison
g.text: Interaction matrix. Mark the empty cells. A blank proves nothing.
THE FOUR RULES THAT DO THE WORK
One page. The size limit IS the edit.
A document with no limit never decides what matters.
One page per SYSTEM, not per game.
Expect a hundred of them over a project, not one.
A paragraph describing how three things connect
is a diagram you have not drawn yet.
If nobody can be wrong about it, it will never be corrected.
Specific numbers and drawn relationships can be contradicted. That is the point.
THE FIVE QUESTIONS, FROM THE BOX ABOVE
1 · Who is here, and what are they trying to finish?
2 · What must be visible without a click?
3 · What is allowed to be one click away?
4 · What must never steal focus or interrupt?

g.inkscape:label: 99 Footer
